claims.claim: 200 small inserts a second is modest... a trimmed Spring Boot app handles it
claims.measured: Single-row Postgres query: 7,668 req/s (java-spring) and 12,731 req/s (java-spring-vt) on 1 CPU
claims.why: Measured Spring Boot database throughput on one CPU is about 38–64 times the 200/s required, so 'handles it' holds.

claims.measured: Go peak memory 11–16 MB vs Spring Boot 209–500 MB; Go image 85–92 MB vs 287 MB
claims.why: Go used about 20–40 times less memory than Spring Boot in every test, which is the direction the claim gives.

claims.claim: Go: about 30–50 MB for this workload
claims.measured: Peak memory 11–12 MB (database tests), 15–16 MB (I/O wait), 2 MB idle
claims.why: Measured Go memory for database-backed work is 11–12 MB, so even the low end of 30 MB is about 2.5 times too high.
A start-up of about a quarter of a second is close enough to 'instant'.

claims.claim: Spring Boot native image (GraalVM): far lower memory and fast startup
claims.why: No GraalVM native-image build was measured.
None of these frameworks were benchmarked.

claims.claim: Node is slower per core than Spring Boot
claims.measured: Plaintext: fastify 40,730 / express 17,601 vs spring 13,653; JSON: fastify 37,277 vs spring 27,264; single DB query: fastify 9,423 / express 9,034 vs spring 7,668 (spring-vt 12,731)
claims.why: Node matched or beat plain Spring Boot in most tests (Fastify was about 3 times faster on plaintext), so the claim mostly points the wrong way.

claims.claim: Python is slower per core than Spring Boot
claims.measured: Single DB query: fastapi 3,706 / flask 1,529–2,119 vs spring 7,668–12,731; JSON: fastapi 6,732 vs spring 27,264
claims.why: Python servers measured well below Spring Boot in every test.

claims.claim: Node and Python use more memory than Spring Boot
claims.measured: Node 55–77 MB and Python 41–123 MB peak vs Spring Boot 209–500 MB peak
claims.why: Node and Python used about 3–10 times less memory than Spring Boot, the opposite of the claim.

claims.claim: Spring Boot's total memory (heap, metaspace, threads, JIT) often lands at 300–400 MB
claims.measured: Peak 209–374 MB in HTTP and CPU tests, 307–500 MB in database tests; 131–134 MB idle
claims.why: Measured peaks under load fall in or near the 300–400 MB range.

claims.claim: CPU may bind before memory does
claims.measured: 7,668–12,731 req/s at about 100% of 1 CPU for a single-row query (about 2–3% CPU at 200/s); peak memory 307–499 MB against 512 MB
claims.why: At 200 req/s Spring Boot would use only a few percent of one CPU while its memory approaches the 512 MB limit, so memory binds first, not CPU.

claims.claim: Startup can take 20–40 seconds, so every deploy is a short outage
claims.why: Measured start-up on one CPU was about 6 s, so 20–40 s is more than 3 times too high.
